## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the manifest refactor keeps runtime behavior on a correctly installed system. Both commands read `install/omarchy-preinstalls.packages` and pass `omarchy-pkg-add` / `omarchy-pkg-drop` the same 13 packages, in the same order, as the previous hardcoded lists. A missing manifest stops both commands before any helper runs. The runtime PKGBUILDs copy the whole `install/` tree to `/usr/share/omarchy/install/` in the same package as `bin/`, so a package built from this change ships the manifest together with the scripts that read it.

Two issues and a rebase note follow.

### `preinstalls-test.sh` depends on the caller's `OMARCHY_PATH`

The scripts now read `$OMARCHY_PATH/install/omarchy-preinstalls.packages`, but the test exports only `PATH`, `HOME` and `OMARCHY_TEST_PKG_LOG`. `base-test.sh` and `test/shell` do not set `OMARCHY_PATH` either.

| `OMARCHY_PATH` when the test runs | Result at this head |
|---|---|
| set to the checkout | passes |
| unset (clean CI, container) | aborts at the first script call: `Preinstall package list not found: /install/omarchy-preinstalls.packages`, with no named failing assertion |
| an installed Omarchy without the manifest | same abort |
| an installed Omarchy with a different manifest | tests the installed manifest, not the checkout |

At the merge-base, and on current `quattro`, the test passes with `OMARCHY_PATH` unset, so this dependency is new.

**Impact:** test-only. The test result depends on the environment rather than the change under test. `docs/testing.md` expects tests to run against `OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT"`.

**Suggested change:** add `export OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT"` next to the `HOME` export, as `default-agent-test.sh` already does.

### An empty or unreadable manifest reports success without changing packages

`[[ -f ... ]]` checks only that the file exists. A comments-only file yields an empty array. A `sed` read failure inside the process substitution is not detected and also yields an empty array.

```text
restore: omarchy-pkg-add (no args) -> returns 0 without calling pacman
         -> opt-out marker removed, exit 0, nothing reinstalled
remove:  web apps/TUIs removed, marker written
         -> omarchy-pkg-drop (no args) -> nothing dropped, exit 0
```

This was observed in an isolated sandbox with the real `omarchy-pkg-add` / `omarchy-pkg-drop` and stubbed `pacman`/`sudo`, for a comments-only and for a mode-000 manifest. With the literal lists at the merge-base this state could not occur. The shipped manifest is well formed, so this needs a damaged package file or a local edit.

The parser also keeps leading and trailing whitespace and a trailing CR as part of a name. In the same sandbox, `omarchy-pkg-drop` silently skipped `obsidian ` (trailing space) and `kdenlive\r` and exited 0 after removing the other 11.

**Impact:** a bad manifest produces a success exit, and on restore also removes the opt-out marker, without reinstalling anything.

**Suggested change:** before any action, fail when the file is unreadable, when the parse fails, or when it yields no packages. Also strip surrounding whitespace and CR while parsing, for example `-e 's/\r$//' -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//'`.

**Optional test improvement:** the new "Install and Remove Preinstalls consume the manifest" assertion compares logged arguments with the checked-in manifest. The merge-base scripts, with their hardcoded lists, pass all 13 assertions when the head manifest is placed beside them, so the assertion does not show that the scripts read the file. Pointing `OMARCHY_PATH` at a temporary tree with a changed fixture manifest, and asserting that both commands log exactly those names, would. The new failure detail also prints a literal `\n`, because `"...\nmanifest: ..."` is inside double quotes.

### Rebase onto current `quattro`

The branch conflicts with current `quattro` (`c3e67f5d`) in `bin/omarchy-remove-preinstalls`. Upstream `7eb818e3` removed the Hermes `omarchy-install-hermes-cli --owns` block directly above the `omarchy-pkg-drop` list this PR replaces. `test/shell.d/preinstalls-test.sh` merges automatically and loses its Hermes cases, so the test would not catch the block coming back.

**Suggested change:** resolve the conflict by keeping upstream's removal of the Hermes block and using `omarchy-pkg-drop "${preinstall_packages[@]}"`. A trial merge resolved this way passes the merged preinstalls test when `OMARCHY_PATH` points at the checkout. The manifest still matches current `quattro`'s lists, and all 13 entries remain in `install/omarchy-base.packages`.

**Optional:** the manifest header says "Keep this list in sync with the packages users can restore", which is circular now that this file is that list. The test's actual rule, that every entry must also be in `install/omarchy-base.packages`, would be more useful there.

**Test scope:** source review of head `7daebfc3` against merge-base `d174d4aa` and current `quattro` `c3e67f5d`. `preinstalls-test.sh` and both commands ran in an isolated sandbox with stubbed package managers and a fake home, including a trial merge onto current `quattro`. The public `omarchy-pkgs` PKGBUILDs and `omarchy-iso` builder scripts were read, not built. The full test suite, real `pacman`, published packages or ISOs and a live system were not exercised.
